title: Countdown tally - personal notes
summary: Personal prep and run-of-show notes for weekly release train sync. Quick checklist, owners, known unknowns, and follow-ups to bring to the meeting.
body:
Context: weekly cadence for the November release train. This is my personal tally to use in the 1:1 prebrief and to update the ops channel after the sync.

Agenda I want to cover:
- Quick status (90s each): infra, serving-runtime, console, QA, security signoff
- Go/No-go checklist review + any hold blockers
- Canary plan confirmation and rollback criteria
- Communication plan: customer notifications + internal incident channel owners
- Action item assignment & owners (explicit)

Quick status notes (scratchy):
- Infra: autoscaler tuning appears stable in staging; still seeing occasional pod OOMs on long sequences. Root cause: memory knob on kv-cache not honored by older model variant. Patch in PR 2147, needs perf run.
- Serving-runtime: kernel scheduling patch merged but not yet on dedicated. Need canary on two GPU nodes. Ask SRE for rollout window.
- Console: rollout UI changes live in staging; billing metrics delayed ~10m (expected).
- QA: regression suite flagged 3 low-prob prompts with hallucination increase (sensitive templates). Triage in progress.
- Security: KMS integration smoke passed, awaiting audit log retention confirmation from compliance.

Go/No-go checklist (my view, call during meeting):
- Data plane stability: YES (staging perf within SLOs after short soak)
- Canary deploy plan in place: YES but needs SRE slot (owner: Jon Kim)
- Known regressions triaged: PARTIAL (owner: Sofia Martinez)
- Security/compliance signoff: PENDING (owner: Marcus Liu from security)
- Customer comms drafted: YES (product)
- Rollback tested: NO (manual rollback verified but automated policy not exercised)

Critical open questions to escalate now:
1) Do we require a hard freeze on new model versions during canary window? (Pros/cons: reduces churn vs blocks urgent fixes)
2) Can SRE reserve 09:00-11:00 PT on Thurs for canary and immediate rollback if needed?
3) When do we flip metrics to 90d retention for billing analytics? Ops needs a 24h heads-up.

Immediate actions (my personal TODOs to update post-meeting):
- Ask Jon to file a small runbook stub for the manual rollback steps and link to runbook page (due: 2025-11-26)
- Ping Marcus for compliance ETA and whether we can proceed with conditional go (due: 2025-11-25)
- Attach failing prompts from regression suite to REL-789 and assign to QA for triage (Sofia)
- Schedule a 30m post-rollout postmortem slot in calendar (tentative)

Notes-to-self for meeting delivery:
- Keep the go/no-go framing binary at the top; avoid rehashing low-impact items if we can defer
- Call out rollback criteria explicitly: 5xx rate > 1% for 2m OR latency p95 > 1.5s sustained for 3m
- Confirm comms channel: #prod-ops for internal, customer-email draft (product) for external

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: KV-cache memory knob not applied to legacy variant -> OOM in long-seq workloads. Mitigation: pin traffic away from legacy variant during canary; urgent patch in PR 2147.
- Risk: Regression prompts not fully triaged -> potential quality incidents post-launch. Mitigation: gate small % of users via canary traffic, add quick rollback toggle.
- Risk: Audit-log retention not confirmed -> blocks full private deployment for a few customers. Mitigation: conditional rollout without private customers until retention verified.

Follow-ups to write into ops channel after sync (short bullets):
- Confirmed: canary window requested Thu 09:00-11:00 PT (pending SRE slot)
- Jon to own rollback runbook link; Sofia to triage regression prompts in REL-789
- Compliance (Marcus) to advise by EOD on retention; conditional go if yes
- Post-rollout postmortem provisional invite sent

Random scratchpad thoughts (do not read aloud unless asked):
- Consider adding a small synthetic probe that hits the long-seq path every 10m during canary (cheap and will catch OOMs earlier)
- If metrics retention flip is risky, we can keep billing metrics separate from observability ingest during initial rollout

Endnotes: keep this doc as personal tally. After meeting: convert to tidy action items and post as short thread in #release-train.

--Priya
